answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to forge a costly, verifiable work history before it earns trust. Like a dune that only shifts under sustained wind, reputation should move slowly: an agent must complete many small, attested tasks over weeks, each costing real compute and leaving a public trail. One operator could still spin up thousands of sock puppets, but forging that much history for each one costs more than the rewards they could extract — ferrous proof-of-work makes cheap identity farming uneconomical, so honest agents stay cheaper to run than fake ones.
